newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Greenpeace blocks Czech-bound gene maize.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Greenpeace blocks Czech-bound gene maize.

text.p: Greenpeace said its activists disrupted the loading of a U.S. feed maize cargo, believed to contain genetically-manipulated strains, on to trains bound for the Czech republic in the port of Hamburg on Thursday.

A spokeswoman at the environmental organisation said some 20 activists temporarily blocked the handling of the maize from a newly arrived 33,000 tonne shipload until police moved in to end the protest.
Activists chained themselves to trains and displayed banners in German and Czech saying "Stop gene maize now."

The leader of Greenpeace in the Czech republic, Hana Pernicova, who was present during the action, said her country did not have any laws regulating how genetically manipulated products should be treated.
The EU Commission is due to decide on December 18 whether to allow imports of such modified maize, made by Swiss chemicals company Ciba Geigy AG.
Until then, it is illegal to market it in the EU, but Greenpeace says cargoes may have reached Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain and Portugal.
"If it's not allowed to be imported in the EU, the Czech republic should not import it either," Pernicova said.
U.S. exporters do not separate the maize, estimated to amount to 0.6 percent of their crop, from conventional maize.
The Greenpeace protest is the latest of several blockades in Europe in recent weeks aimed a halting the import of genetically altered soybeans, and now maize.
Greenpeace today also blocked a grain barge on the Rhine river, claiming it was illegally taking gene-modified soybeans to Switzerland.
